newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish PM asks for agriculture minister's dismissal.
newsitem.headline: Polish PM asks for agriculture minister's dismissal.

text.p: Poland's prime minister asked the president on Friday to recall Agriculture Minister Roman Jagielinski from his post, the presidential press office said.
It said in a statement that President Aleksander Kwasniewski will dismiss the minister after the head of state returns from his official visit to Italy on April 8.

Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz was forced to fire Jagielinski, a leader of the more market-oriented fraction in the co-ruling Polish Peasant Party (PSL), after he lost the support of the majority of the group's leadership.
The majority -- led by Peasants' president Waldemar Pawlak, who represents small farm owners keen to uphold state protection of agriculture -- have attacked Jagielinski's farm policies.
Pawlak's supporters accused him of allowing a large food trade deficit, and of harming Polish farmers, who have been hoarding grain and waiting for prices to rise, by allowing grain imports.
Jagielinski came under fire from many of his colleagues after he lost the race for party leader late last year to Pawlak.
In February the PSL's council revoked its backing for Jagielinski as agriculture minister and recommended he be replaced by a little-known Pawlak supporter, Jaroslaw Kalinowski.
But Premier Cimoszewicz, a member of the senior ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD), has been delaying the sacking of Jagielinski, apparently reluctant to accept Kalinowski.
